notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-27: 1897 report is the second report in volume annualreportlig02statgoog (fiscal 1897, which text says 'urgently required'); contract date and crib status now from the 1901 report. Omaha Bee says the ice was firm at the start while Superior Times says soft and mushy: both stated in story. Bulletin 1914 volume gives Dissett's tow on 31 October with no year stated in the notice; LighthouseFriends says 1915. Mary F. Hayden vs Hayden's wife Mary (named in the Superior Times) not linked. USCG roster lines (1943 onward) deliberately left out under the living-people rule. NRHP 83002005 nomination is not digitised, so no NRHP citation. Light-House Board reports for 1902-1904 are not in the corpus, so the lighting date (23 May 1904), lens, and fog signal come from LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; facts only). USLHS places the station 1.7 km from the record position; USLHS rounds to the minute, no correction proposed. Newspapers differ on days Bernor was alone (six vs seven); LighthouseFriends calls Joe Bernor an assistant but 1908 papers call him Hayden's cousin (spelled Bernor/Berner). A Bamberg Herald page dated 1908-09-05 retells the recovery of Hayden's body over the ice (likely misdated); not used. Mary F. Hayden (first assistant 1905) not tied to Delos Hayden by any source. Dissett's rescue: Bulletin 1914 volume vs LighthouseFriends' 1915; a second Bulletin 1916 p.50 notice (food and tow) is dated 31 October by the Bulletin while LighthouseFriends says 1917; not used in story. Dock history differs: LF says lift dock 2008, lost April 2009, rebuilt by 2011, lost to storm 2015; society says dock destroyed in a northeaster (2010 on home page). Deed year: LF April 2007, City Paper 'since 2006'. Fog signal: 1901 report says steam, LF says oil engines (as built). Hayden's 'only companion' details from newspapers OCR; names OCR-read.
